points.heading: Deepen: one-word times
points.body:
Today we stay on the one-word path only (no haber). Keep the thread: verb = action; conjugate = change for who/when; stem = fixed part; ending = tip.

Let's explore together. Review the five clocks as one story: present, imperfect, preterite, future, conditional. The helpful contrast is cantaba (leaves the event open) versus canté (closes it).

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write five sentences with fixed frames — today / when I was little / yesterday / tomorrow / if I could — same verb, different time. Name the time and say why it fits.

Common mistake: «Ayer iba al cine» when you mean you went and finished → «Ayer fui al cine».

lesson.summary: This lesson teaches practice one-word times. Understand the central idea first, then explore it, practice it, and check a common mistake.

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What two parts make a compound tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
It is always a future word.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
